label_source: Used in the verse as பணியும்
Claude's label; not the verses' word

author: கணியன் பூங்குன்றன்
quote: யாதும் ஊரே ; யாவரும் கேளிர் ;

author: கணியன் பூங்குன்றன்
quote: நீர்வழிப் படூஉம் புணைபோல, ஆருயிர்

author: கணியன் பூங்குன்றன்
quote: முறைவழிப் படூஉம்’ என்பது திறவோர்

author: கணியன் பூங்குன்றன்
quote: பெரியோரை வியத்தலும் இலமே;

author: கணியன் பூங்குன்றன்
quote: சிறியோரை இகழ்தல் அதனினும் இலமே.
பழவினையும் அன்ன தகைத்தேதற் செய்த
உறற்பால நீக்கல் உறுவர்க்கும் ஆகா,
மம்மர் அறுக்கும் மருந்து.
கடைநிலத்தோ ராயினும், கற்றறிந் தோரைத்
கல்வி கரையில கற்பவர் நாள்சில
காணிற் கடைப்பட்டான் என்றிகழார் - காணாய்
நகலின் இனிதாயின் காண்பாம் அகல்வானத்(து)
வான்றோய் குடிப்பிறந்தார்க் கல்லது - வான்றோயும்

author: இளங்கோ அடிகள்
quote: ஊழ்வினை உருத்துவந்து ஊட்டும் என்பதூஉம்

author: இளங்கோ அடிகள்
quote: கோவலன் பண்டை ஊழ்வினை உருத்தென்.

author: பரிமேலழகர்
quote: எல்லாம் வழியாக வருதலுடைமையின், ஊழே வலியது என்பதாம்.

author: பரிமேலழகர்
quote: சிவிகை பொறுத்தானோடு ஊர்ந்தான் இடை-சிவிகையைக் காவுவானோடு செலுத்துவானிடைக் காட்சியளவை தன்னானே உணரப்படும்.

author: மணக்குடவர்
quote: எல்லா வுயிர்க்கும் பிறப்பால் ஒரு வேறுபாடில்லை

author: பரிமேலழகர்
quote: அச்செயல் அவன் யாக்கையோடு கூடும் நாள் வரும் வழியை வாராமல் அடைக்குங் கல்லாம்.
சிறப்பு ஈனும் செல்வமும் ஈனும் அறத்தினூஉங்கு ஆக்கம் எவனோ உயிர்க்கு

couplet: It yields distinction, yields prosperity; what gain
Greater than virtue can a living man obtain?
pope.gloss: Virtue will confer heaven and wealth; what greater source of happiness can man possess ?

quote: அறத்தினூஉங்கு ஆக்கமும் இல்லை அதனை மறத்தலின் ஊங்கில்லை கேடு

couplet: No greater gain than virtue aught can cause;
No greater loss than life oblivious of her laws.
pope.gloss: There can be no greater source of good than (the practice of) virtue; there can be no greater source of evil than the forgetfulness of it.

quote: ஒல்லும் வகையான் அறவினை ஓவாதே செல்லும்வாய் எல்லாஞ் செயல்

couplet: To finish virtue's work with ceaseless effort strive,
What way thou may'st, where'er thou see'st the work may thrive.
pope.gloss: As much as possible, in every way, incessantly practise virtue.

quote: மனத்துக்கண் மாசிலன் ஆதல் அனைத்து அறன் ஆகுல நீர பிற

couplet: Spotless be thou in mind! This only merits virtue's name;
All else, mere pomp of idle sound, no real worth can claim.
pope.gloss: Let him who does virtuous deeds be of spotless mind; to that extent is virtue; all else is vain show.

quote: அழுக்காறு அவாவெகுளி இன்னாச்சொல் நான்கும் இழுக்கா இயன்றது அறம்

couplet: 'Tis virtue when, his footsteps sliding not through envy, wrath,
Lust, evil speech-these four, man onwards moves in ordered path.
pope.gloss: That conduct is virtue which is free from these four things, viz, malice, desire, anger and bitter speech.

quote: அன்றறிவாம் என்னாது அறஞ்செய்க மற்றது பொன்றுங்கால் பொன்றாத் துணை

couplet: Do deeds of virtue now. Say not, 'To-morrow we'll be wise';
Thus, when thou diest, shalt thou find a help that never dies.
pope.gloss: Defer not virtue to another day; receive her now; and at the dying hour she will be your undying friend.

quote: அறத்தாறு இதுவென வேண்டா சிவிகை பொறுத்தானோடு ஊர்ந்தான் இடை

couplet: Needs not in words to dwell on virtue's fruits: compare
The man in litter borne with them that toiling bear!
pope.gloss: The fruit of virtue need not be described in books; it may be inferred from seeing the bearer of a palanquin and the rider therein.

quote: வீழ்நாள் படாஅமை நன்றாற்றின் அஃதொருவன் வாழ்நாள் வழியடைக்கும் கல்

couplet: If no day passing idly, good to do each day you toil,
A stone it will be to block the way of future days of moil.
pope.gloss: If one allows no day to pass without some good being done, his conduct will be a stone to block up the passage to other births.

quote: அறத்தான் வருவதே இன்பம் மற் றெல்லாம் புறத்த புகழும் இல

couplet: What from virtue floweth, yieldeth dear delight;
All else extern, is void of glory's light.
pope.gloss: Only that pleasure which flows from domestic virtue is pleasure; all else is not pleasure, and it is without praise.

quote: செயற்பால தோரும் அறனே ஒருவற்கு உயற்பால தோரும் பழி

couplet: 'Virtue' sums the things that should be done;
'Vice' sums the things that man should shun.
pope.gloss: That is virtue which each ought to do, and that is vice which each should shun.

quote: ஆகூழால் தோன்றும் அசைவின்மை கைப்பொருள் போகூழால் தோன்றும் மடி

couplet: Wealth-giving fate power of unflinching effort brings;
From fate that takes away idle remissness springs.
pope.gloss: Perseverance comes from a prosperous fate, and idleness from an adverse fate.

quote: பேதைப் படுக்கும் இழவூழ் அறிவகற்றும் ஆகலூழ் உற்றக் கடை

couplet: The fate that loss ordains makes wise men's wisdom foolishness;
The fate that gain bestows with ampler powers will wisdom bless.
pope.gloss: An adverse fate produces folly, and a prosperous fate produces enlarged knowledge.

quote: நுண்ணிய நூல்பல கற்பினும் மற்றுந்தன் உண்மை யறிவே மிகும்

couplet: In subtle learning manifold though versed man be,
'The wisdom, truly his, will gain supremacy.
pope.gloss: Although (a man) may study the most polished treatises, the knowledge which fate has decreed to him will still prevail.

quote: இருவேறு உலகத்து இயற்கை திருவேறு தெள்ளிய ராதலும் வேறு

couplet: Two fold the fashion of the world: some live in fortune's light;
While other some have souls in wisdom's radiance bright.
pope.gloss: There are (through fate) two different natures in the world, hence the difference (observable in men) in (their acquisition of) wealth, and in their attainment of knowledge.

quote: நல்லவை எல்லாஅந் தீயவாம் தீயவும் நல்லவாம் செல்வம் செயற்கு

couplet: All things that good appear will oft have ill success;
All evil things prove good for gain of happiness.
pope.gloss: In the acquisition of property, every thing favourable becomes unfavourable, and (on the other hand) everything unfavourable becomes favourable, (through the power of fate).

quote: பரியினும் ஆகாவாம் பாலல்ல உய்த்துச் சொரியினும் போகா தம

couplet: Things not your own will yield no good, howe'er you guard with pain;
Your own, howe'er you scatter them abroad, will yours remain.
pope.gloss: Whatever is not conferred by fate cannot be preserved although it be guarded with most painful care; and that, which fate has made his, cannot be lost, although one should even take it and throw it away.

quote: வகுத்தான் வகுத்த வகையல்லால் கோடி தொகுத்தார்க்கு துய்த்தல் அரிது

couplet: Save as the 'sharer' shares to each in due degree,
To those who millions store enjoyment scarce can be.
pope.gloss: Even those who gather together millions will only enjoy them, as it has been determined by the disposer (of all things).

quote: துறப்பார்மன் துப்புர வில்லார் உறற்பால ஊட்டா கழியு மெனின்

couplet: The destitute with ascetics merit share,
If fate to visit with predestined ills would spare.
pope.gloss: The destitute will renounce desire (and become ascetics), if (fate) do not make them suffer the hindrances to which they are liable, and they pass away.

quote: நன்றாங்கால் நல்லவாக் காண்பவர் அன்றாங்கால் அல்லற் படுவ தெவன்?

couplet: When good things come, men view them all as gain;
When evils come, why then should they complain?
pope.gloss: How is it that those, who are pleased with good fortune, trouble themselves when evil comes, (since both are equally the decree of fa te) ?

quote: ஊழிற் பெருவலி யாவுள மற்றொன்று சூழினுந் தான்முந் துறும்

couplet: What powers so great as those of Destiny? Man's skill
Some other thing contrives; but fate's beforehand still.
pope.gloss: What is stronger than fate ? If we think of an expedient (to avert it), it will itself be with us before (the thought).

quote: கற்க கசடறக் கற்பவை கற்றபின் நிற்க அதற்குத் தக

couplet: So learn that you may full and faultless learning gain,
Then in obedience meet to lessons learnt remain.
pope.gloss: Let a man learn thoroughly whatever he may learn, and let his conduct be worthy of his learning.

quote: எண்ணென்ப ஏனை எழுத்தென்ப இவ்விரண் டும் கண்ணென்ப வாழும் உயிர்க்கு

couplet: The twain that lore of numbers and of letters give
Are eyes, the wise declare, to all on earth that live.
pope.gloss: Letters and numbers are the two eyes of man.

quote: கண்ணுடையர் என்பவர் கற்றோர் முகத்திரண்டு புண்ணுடையர் கல்லா தவர்

couplet: Men who learning gain have eyes, men say;
Blockheads' faces pairs of sores display.
pope.gloss: The learned are said to have eyes, but the unlearned have (merely) two sores in their face.

quote: உவப்பத் தலைக்கூடி உள்ளப் பிரிதல் அனைத்தே புலவர் தொழில்

couplet: You meet with joy, with pleasant thought you part;
Such is the learned scholar's wonderous art!
pope.gloss: It is the part of the learned to give joy to those whom they meet, and on leaving, to make them think (Oh! when shall we meet them again.)

quote: உடையார்முன் இல்லார்போல் ஏக்கற்றுங் கற்றார் கடையரே கல்லா தவர்

couplet: With soul submiss they stand, as paupers front a rich man's face;
Yet learned men are first; th'unlearned stand in lowest place.
pope.gloss: The unlearned are inferior to the learned, before whom they stand begging, as the destitute before the wealthy.

quote: தொட்டனைத் தூறும் மணற்கேணி மாந்தர்க்குக் கற்றனைத் தூறும் அறிவு

couplet: In sandy soil, when deep you delve, you reach the springs below;
The more you learn, the freer streams of wisdom flow.
pope.gloss: Water will flow from a well in the sand in proportion to the depth to which it is dug, and knowledge will flow from a man in proportion to his learning.

quote: யாதானும் நாடாமால் ஊராமால் என்னொருவன் சாந்துணையுங் கல்லாத வாறு

couplet: The learned make each land their own, in every city find a home;
Who, till they die; learn nought, along what weary ways they roam!
pope.gloss: How is it that any one can remain without learning, even to his death, when (to the learned man) every country is his own (country), and every town his own (town) ?

quote: ஒருமைக்கண் தான் கற்ற கல்வி ஒருவற்கு எழுமையும் ஏமாப் புடைத்து

couplet: The man who store of learning gains,
In one, through seven worlds, bliss attains.
pope.gloss: The learning, which a man has acquired in one birth, will yield him pleasure during seven births.

quote: தாமின் புறுவது உலகின் புறக் கண்டு காமுறுவர் கற்றறிந் தார்

couplet: Their joy is joy of all the world, they see; thus more
The learners learn to love their cherished lore.
pope.gloss: The learned will long (for more learning), when they see that while it gives pleasure to themselves, the world also derives pleasure from it.

quote: கேடில் விழுச்செல்வம் கல்வி யொருவற்கு மாடல்ல மற்றை யவை

couplet: Learning is excellence of wealth that none destroy;
To man nought else affords reality of joy.
pope.gloss: Learning is the true imperishable riches; all other things are not riches.

quote: ஒளிஒருவற்கு உள்ள வெறுக்கை இளிஒருவற்கு அஃதிறந்து வாழ்தும் எனல்

couplet: The light of life is mental energy; disgrace is his
Who says, 'I 'ill lead a happy life devoid of this.'
pope.gloss: One's light is the abundance of one's courage; one's darkness is the desire to live destitute of such (a state of mind.)

quote: பிறப்பொக்கும் எல்லா உயிர்க்கும் சிறப்பொவ்வா செய்தொழில் வேற்றுமை யான்

couplet: All men that live are one in circumstances of birth;
Diversities of works give each his special worth.
pope.gloss: All human beings agree as regards their birth but differ as regards their characteristics, because of the different qualities of their actions.

quote: மேலிருந்தும் மேலல்லார் மேலல்லர் கீழிருந்தும் கீழல்லார் கீழல் லவர்

couplet: The men of lofty line, whose souls are mean, are never great
The men of lowly birth, when high of soul, are not of low estate.
pope.gloss: Though (raised) above, the base cannot become great; though (brought) low, the great cannot become base.

quote: ஒருமை மகளிரே போலப் பெருமையும் தன்னைத்தான் கொண்டொழுகின் உண்டு

couplet: Like single-hearted women, greatness too,
Exists while to itself is true.
pope.gloss: Even greatness, like a woman's chastity, belongs only to him who guards himself.

quote: பெருமை யுடையவர் ஆற்றுவார் ஆற்றின் அருமை உடைய செயல்

couplet: The man endowed with greatness true,
Rare deeds in perfect wise will do.
pope.gloss: (Though reduced) the great will be able to perform, in the proper way, deeds difficult (for others to do).

quote: சிறியார் உணர்ச்சியுள் இல்லை பெரியாரைப் பேணிக் கொள் வேம் என்னும் நோக்கு

couplet: 'As votaries of the truly great we will ourselves enroll,'
Is thought that enters not the mind of men of little soul.
pope.gloss: It is never in the nature of the base to seek the society of the great and partake of their nature.

quote: இறப்பே புரிந்த தொழிற்றாம் சிறப்புந்தான் சீரல் லவர்கண் படின்

couplet: Whene'er distinction lights on some unworthy head,
Then deeds of haughty insolence are bred.
pope.gloss: Even nobility of birth, wealth and learning, if in (the possession of) the base, will (only) produce everincreasing pride.

quote: பணியுமாம் என்றும் பெருமை சிறுமை அணியுமாம் தன்னை வியந்து

couplet: Greatness humbly bends, but littleness always
Spreads out its plumes, and loads itself with praise.
pope.gloss: The great will always humble himself; but the mean will exalt himself in self-admiration.

quote: பெருமை பெருமிதம் இன்மை சிறுமை பெருமிதம் ஊர்ந்து விடல்

couplet: Greatness is absence of conceit; meanness, we deem,
Riding on car of vanity supreme.
pope.gloss: Freedom from conceit is (the nature of true) greatness; (while) obstinacy therein is (that of) meanness.

quote: அற்றம் மறைக்கும் பெருமை சிறுமைதான் குற்றமே கூறி விடும்

couplet: Greatness will hide a neighbour's shame;
Meanness his faults to all the world proclaim.
pope.gloss: The great hide the faults of others; the base only divulge them.

quote: இருநோக்கு இவளுண்கண் உள்ளது ஒருநோக்கு நோய்நோக்கொன் றந்நோய் மருந்து

couplet: A double witchery have glances of her liquid eye;
One glance is glance that brings me pain; the other heals again.
pope.gloss: There are two looks in the dyed eyes of this (fair one); one causes pain, and the other is the cure thereof.

quote: கண்களவு கொள்ளும் சிறுநோக்கம் காமத்தில் செம்பாகம் அன்று பெரிது

couplet: The furtive glance, that gleams one instant bright,
Is more than half of love's supreme delight.
pope.gloss: A single stolen glance of her eyes is more than half the pleasure (of sexual embrace).

quote: நோக்கினாள் நோக்கி இறைஞ்சினாள் அஃதவள் யாப்பினுள் அட்டிய நீர்

couplet: She looked, and looking drooped her head:
On springing shoot of love 'its water shed!
pope.gloss: She has looked (at men) and stooped (her head); and that (sign) waters as it were (the corn of) our love.

quote: யான்நோக்கும் காலை நிலன்நோக்கும் நோக்காக்கால் தான்நோக்கி மெல்ல நகும்

couplet: I look on her: her eyes are on the ground the while:
I look away: she looks on me with timid smile.
pope.gloss: When I look, she looks down; when I do not, she looks and smiles gently.

quote: குறிக்கொண்டு நோக்காமை அல்லால் ஒருகண் சிறக்கணித்தாள் போல நகும்

couplet: She seemed to see me not; but yet the maid
Her love, by smiling side-long glance, betrayed.
pope.gloss: She not only avoids a direct look at me, but looks as it were with a half-closed eye and smiles.

quote: உறாஅ தவர்போல் சொலினும் செறாஅர்சொல் ஒல்லை உணரப் படும்

couplet: Though with their lips affection they disown,
Yet, when they hate us not, 'tis quickly known.
pope.gloss: Though they may speak harshly as if they were strangers, the words of the friendly are soon understood.

quote: செறாஅச் சிறுசொல்லும் செற்றார்போல் நோக்கும் உறாஅர்போன்று உற்றார் குறிப்பு

couplet: The slighting words that anger feign, while eyes their love reveal.
Are signs of those that love, but would their love conceal.
pope.gloss: Little words that are harsh and looks that are hateful are (but) the expressions of lovers who wish to act like strangers.

quote: அசையியற்கு உண்டாண்டோ ர் ஏஎர்யான் நோக்கப் பசையினள் பைய நகும்

couplet: I gaze, the tender maid relents the while;
And, oh the matchless grace of that soft smile!
pope.gloss: When I look, the pitying maid looks in return and smiles gently; and that is a comforting sign for me.

quote: ஏதிலார் போலப் பொதுநோக்கு நோக்குதல் காதலார் கண்ணே உள

couplet: The look indifferent, that would its love disguise,
Is only read aright by lovers' eyes.
pope.gloss: Both the lovers are capable of looking at each other in an ordinary way, as if they were perfect strangers.

quote: கண்ணொடு கண்இணை நோக்கொக்கின் வாய்ச்சொற்கள் என்ன பயனும் இல

couplet: When eye to answering eye reveals the tale of love,
All words that lips can say must useless prove.
pope.gloss: The words of the mouths are of no use whatever, when there is perfect agreement between the eyes (of lovers).

title: Can fate be overcome?
question: How much of a life is fixed, and what remains for effort and attitude?
open_questions: Does ஊழ் in the Kural carry the same karmic sense as பழவினை in the Naladiyar, or is that a later commentators' reading?
Is the raft image in Purananuru 192 fatalism, or a reason for equanimity that needs no moral accounting?

quote: தெய்வத்தான் ஆகா தெனினும் முயற்சிதன் மெய்வருத்தக் கூலி தரும்

couplet: Though fate-divine should make your labour vain;
Effort its labour's sure reward will gain.
pope.gloss: Although it be said that, through fate, it cannot be attained, yet labour, with bodily exertion, will yield its reward.

quote: ஊழையும் உப்பக்கம் காண்பர் உலைவின்றித் தாழாது உஞற்று பவர்

couplet: Who strive with undismayed, unfaltering mind,
At length shall leave opposing fate behind.
pope.gloss: They who labour on, without fear and without fainting will see even fate (put) behind their back.

title: Does birth decide a person's worth?
question: What do the texts say makes a person great, and do they agree with themselves?
open_questions: Should the graph record who benefits from a reading? Modern anti-caste readings and older commentaries may stress different things in the same verse.
Does செய்தொழில் mean deeds or occupation in Kural 972? Pope's 'works' leaves this open.

title: What is learning for, and how far can it take you?
question: Is knowledge earned or innate, and what should it do to a person?
open_questions: Is 373 about innate ability, or about what fate permits? Kalaignar reads natural intelligence, but the verse sits in the chapter on fate.

title: Reading what is not said
question: How do the same skills work in love and in statecraft?
open_questions: Is the parallel between the two chapters deliberate design? The matching titles suggest it but do not prove it.

quote: கூறாமை நோக்கிக் குறிப்பறிவான் எஞ்ஞான்றும் மாறாநீர் வையக் கணி

couplet: Who knows the sign, and reads unuttered thought, the gem is he,
Of earth round traversed by the changeless sea.
pope.gloss: The minister who by looking (at the king) understands his mind without being told (of it), will be a perpetual ornament to the world which is surrounded by a never-drying sea.

quote: அடுத்தது காட்டும் பளிங்குபோல் நெஞ்சம் கடுத்தது காட்டும் முகம்

couplet: As forms around in crystal mirrored clear we find,
The face will show what's throbbing in the mind.
pope.gloss: As the mirror reflects what is near so does the face show what is uppermost in the mind.

quote: பகைமையும் கேண்மையும் கண்ணுரைக்கும் கண்ணின் வகைமை உணர்வார்ப் பெறின்

couplet: The eye speaks out the hate or friendly soul of man;
To those who know the eye's swift varying moods to scan.
pope.gloss: If a king gets ministers who can read the movements of the eye, the eyes (of foreign kings) will (themselves) reveal (to him) their hatred or friendship.

title: One verse, different worldviews
question: How do commentators from different eras change what these verses mean?
open_questions: How far does each reading fit the Tamil itself? A reader of classical Tamil should judge this; it isn't settled by counting commentators.
Does Kalaignar's pattern hold across all 133 chapters? Only a few verses were checked.
